prompt: Start with "If a figure is a square, then it is a rectangle." Now swap the hypothesis and the conclusion to get "If a figure is a rectangle, then it is a square." What is this new statement called?
hint: The three related statements are the converse, the inverse, and the contrapositive. Only one of them is a pure swap.

hints.text: The three related statements are the converse, the inverse, and the contrapositive. Only one of them is a pure swap.
Swapping (with no negating) makes the converse; negating both parts makes the inverse.

explanation: Given "if $p$, then $q$," the converse is "if $q$, then $p$" — the two parts trade places.
Nothing is negated here, so it is not the inverse or the contrapositive.
Notice this converse is FALSE (a rectangle need not be a square), even though the original is true — a converse is a brand-new claim that has to be checked on its own.

alternativeExplanations.title: Converse means "reverse"
steps: Converse and reverse sound alike, and that is the memory hook: the converse reverses the order of the two parts.
Inverse "inverts" (negates) both parts; the contrapositive does both — swap AND negate.
